Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 1) The basic flow of communication starts with:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Communication starts with the sender. The sender prepares and transmits the message. The message then passes through a channel to the receiver.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 2) Communication becomes complete when the receiver gives:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Feedback completes communication. It tells the sender whether the message was understood. It also helps correct misunderstanding.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 3) In communication, the medium through which message is sent is called:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Channel is the medium of communication. Examples include speech, writing, radio, television or posters. A poor channel may distort the message.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 4) In communication process, the person who receives the message is:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Receiver is the person or group who gets the message. The receiver interprets the message. Feedback from receiver completes the process.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 5) The first response of receiver in behaviour change sequence is:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: The sequence begins with awareness. The receiver first becomes aware of the message. Then interest, evaluation and adoption may follow.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 6) In the response sequence, awareness is followed by:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: After awareness, the receiver develops interest. Interest means the person wants to know more. This may later lead to evaluation and adoption.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 7) The final step in the response sequence shown in the file is:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Adoption is the final step of the sequence. It means the person accepts the idea or behaviour. In health education, adoption means behaviour change.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 8) One-way communication is best represented by:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: One-way communication has no feedback from receiver. Lecture and announcement are examples. It is less interactive than two-way communication.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 9) Two-way communication is best represented by:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Two-way communication includes interaction and feedback. Discussion and interview are examples. It is better for clearing doubt and misunderstanding.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 10) Verbal communication means use of:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Verbal communication uses spoken or written words. Speeches, conversations and letters are examples. It may be oral or written.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 11) Body language, facial expression and posture are examples of:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Non-verbal communication occurs without words. It includes body language, facial expression, posture and gestures. It often supports or modifies verbal messages.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 12) Structured official communication is called:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Formal communication is structured and official. Reports, official meetings and memos are examples. It is commonly used in institutions.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 13) Casual unofficial communication is called:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Informal communication is casual and unofficial. Chats, rumors and casual talks are examples. It is not usually part of official reporting.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 14) Personal contact is an example of:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Personal contact is an individual approach. It allows direct interaction with one person. It is useful for counseling and personal advice.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 15) Home visit belongs to:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Home visit is an individual approach. It gives opportunity to understand family and home conditions. It is useful in community health work.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 16) Demonstration is classified under:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Demonstration is a group approach. It teaches by showing a method to a group. It is more practical than lecture alone.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 17) Workshop and seminar are examples of:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Workshop and seminar are group methods. They allow interaction among participants. They are useful for training and discussion.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 18) Television, radio and newspaper are examples of:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Mass approach reaches a large population. Television, radio and newspaper are mass media. They are useful for spreading health messages quickly.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 19) Posters and health exhibitions are methods of:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Posters and exhibitions are mass communication methods. They can reach many people at the same time. They are useful for awareness creation.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 20) Difficulty in hearing is which type of communication barrier?
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Hearing difficulty is a physiological barrier. It affects receiving and understanding the message. Expression difficulty is another physiological barrier.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 21) Emotional disturbance and neurosis are:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Psychological barriers arise from mental or emotional factors. Emotional disturbance, neurosis and low comprehension can interfere with communication. They reduce understanding and acceptance of health messages.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 22) Noise, invisibility and congestion are:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Environmental barriers are due to surroundings. Noise, invisibility and congestion interfere with communication. A poor environment reduces attention and message clarity.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 23) Customs, beliefs and religion may act as:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Cultural barriers arise from customs, beliefs, religion and attitudes. They may affect acceptance of health advice. Health messages should respect local culture.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 24) Illiteracy and low level of understanding are mainly:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Illiteracy and low knowledge are included under cultural barriers in the file. They reduce comprehension of health messages. Simple language and visual methods may help.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 25) Health education may fail mainly due to:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Communication barriers interfere between educator and community. They may be physiological, psychological, environmental or cultural. Removing barriers improves health education.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 26) A personal letter is an example of:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Personal letter is included under individual approach. It is directed to a specific person. It can carry personalized health advice.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 27) Panel discussion is classified as:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Panel discussion is a group method. It involves discussion among selected speakers before an audience. It is useful for presenting different views.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 28) The principle of credibility in health education means:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.option2: Only mass media should be used
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.option3: The message and source should be trustworthy
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: People accept health messages more easily when the source is trusted. Credibility depends on truthfulness, consistency and reputation of the educator. False or exaggerated claims reduce acceptance. A credible message improves behaviour change.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 29) The principle of participation means:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.option1: Only written materials should be used
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.option3: People should actively take part in learning
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Participation makes health education more effective. People learn better when they discuss, ask questions and practise. It changes the audience from passive listeners to active learners. This improves acceptance and retention of health messages.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 30) Motivation in health education mainly helps to:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Motivation is a driving force for action. Health education does not end with giving information. The aim is to motivate people to adopt healthy behaviour. Without motivation, knowledge may not become practice.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 31) Repetition of a health message is related to:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Reinforcement means repeating and strengthening the message. Repeated messages improve memory and acceptance. It is useful because one exposure may not change behaviour. Follow-up education also acts as reinforcement.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 32) The best method for teaching handwashing technique is:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Demonstration is best for teaching a practical skill. The learner can see the exact steps. It is more effective than lecture alone. Handwashing, ORS preparation and breastfeeding positioning are good examples.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 33) Communication without feedback is called:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: One-way communication has no feedback. The sender transmits message but receiver does not respond. Lectures and announcements are examples.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 34) Role play is included under:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Role play is a group method. Participants act out a situation to learn behaviour and communication skills. It is useful for counseling and health education training.

Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.question: 35) Feedback is important because it:
Behavioural Science, Health Communicatio.exp: Feedback tells the sender how the receiver understood the message. It helps detect confusion and error. It makes communication complete and effective.
